Subject: [P0] US-WEST2 AZB — 5xx spike / autosuggest failing (prod)

Vanessa / Redwood team,

We’re seeing a sudden, sustained spike in 5xx errors and latency for Polaris production in us-west2 (AZ B) starting ~08:10 PDT. Search and autosuggest calls are returning 502/504s and timeouts — roughly 40–55% error rate and p95 latency jumped to ~2.6s. Customer pages are degraded; we’re receiving real user complaints.

Attached is a short log dump and a screenshot of the 503s. Can you confirm whether this is an AZ-level infrastructure issue or a routing/load problem on your side? Polaris needs an immediate cross-region reroute to us-east1 if this can’t be contained within the next 15 minutes.

Impact: Production search and personalization are failing; high revenue pages affected.

Regards,
Santiago Ruiz
Polaris — Oncall SRE
ops@polaris.ai

Santiago — thanks for the immediate heads-up and the logs. I’m escalating internally to our SRE and routing teams now (cc’d).

Immediate plan we propose while we triage the AZ:
- SRE (Hannah/Connor) to run the geo-drain to divert production traffic for Polaris to us-east1 (target: start within 10–15m).
- If geo-drain takes longer, enable the degraded model variant and reduced batching on us-east1 to reduce KVCACHE pressure.
- Sales/CS (Marissa) to confirm any credit/contract asks and notify Polaris execs.
- I’ll request executive authorization for temporary routing pinning & up to $20k incremental spend to cover cross-region token/burst costs.

Please confirm: 1) Polaris approves the reroute to us-east1, and 2) whether you want a hard failover (stop serving from us-west2) or a soft steer (weighted routing).

Subject: Re: [P0] US-WEST2 AZB — 5xx spike / autosuggest failing (prod)

Vanessa / team,

We dug into the logs Santiago provided — symptoms match KV cache eviction amplification combined with an AZ-specific NIC flake we’re seeing in the telemetry (packet retries up at the AZ level). That combination explains the burst of 5xxs and high p95 for short sequences.

Technical runbook we will execute as of 08:35 PDT (ETA 10–15m to be routing-effective):
1) Activate geo-steering policy to steer 92% of Polaris prod traffic from us-west2 to us-east1. (soft steer first).
2) Reduce model threading and enable quantized variant on us-east1 for Polaris traffic to reduce memory pressure (expected +10–15% CPU, +~$8k/day estimate under current QPS).
3) Temporarily raise concurrency cap for Polaris on us-east1 to prevent queueing.
4) Monitor for KV cache hit stabilization and tail latency.

Expected customer-visible impact: minor search ranking deltas for 1–2 hours during degraded variant; overall success rate expected to return to >98% within 20–30 minutes of steering.

Playbook links: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/sre/playbooks/geo-drain.pdf

Requesting explicit authorization from Markus for the routing pin and from Sales (Marissa) for any commercial concessions to Polaris.

-Hannah
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: [P0] US-WEST2 AZB — 5xx spike / autosuggest failing (prod)

Santiago / Lena — quick update and closure: we executed the soft geo-steer at 08:36 PDT and increased weight to us-east1 to 92%. Within ~18 minutes the error rate dropped from ~50% to <3% and p95 latency returned to ~320ms. At 09:10 PDT we switched to the quantized model variant on us-east1 to keep memory pressure low; that is holding.

We’ve kept us-west2 in read-only/limited mode for 30 minutes while monitoring; we will only do a hard drain if errors reappear. Markus has authorized the temporary routing and a one-time up to $20k credit for the incident (Markus cc’d).

Next steps:
- Postmortem meeting scheduled for Thu 07/22 10:00 PDT (invite to Polaris and internal stakeholders).
- Marissa will follow up re: any commercial remediation and finalize the credit note.
- SRE to deliver a short RCA and model-tuning recommendations by EOD tomorrow.

Appreciate the quick coordination — we’ll keep you posted in the incident channel and the postmortem.
